video_goal: Demonstrate the step-by-step process of removing and replacing the ceramic disc cartridge in a Hansgrohe Metris faucet.
required_subjects_and_props: Hansgrohe Metris faucet, replacement ceramic disc cartridge, 2.5mm Allen wrench, small metal pick, adjustable wrench, microfiber cloth

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands reach under the sink to turn the two oval water supply valve handles clockwise until they stop.
A metal pick is inserted into the small seam of the red/blue temperature indicator plug on the front of the Hansgrohe Metris faucet handle, popping the plug out.
A 2.5mm Allen wrench is inserted into the exposed hole on the handle and rotated counter-clockwise multiple times.
A hand grasps the flat metal faucet handle and pulls it straight up, separating it from the faucet body.
Fingers grip the smooth, dome-shaped metal cap below the handle and twist it counter-clockwise to remove it.
An adjustable wrench is fitted around the exposed brass retaining nut and pushed counter-clockwise to break it loose.
Fingers spin the loosened brass retaining nut the rest of the way off and lift it out of the frame.
Fingers pinch the plastic stem of the old ceramic disc cartridge and pull it straight up and out of the brass faucet body.
A microfiber cloth is pushed into the empty brass faucet body, wiping the metal base and the two circular water inlet holes.
A hand holds up a new Hansgrohe ceramic disc cartridge, tilting the bottom toward the camera to reveal two protruding plastic alignment pegs.
The new ceramic disc cartridge is lowered into the faucet body, twisting slightly until the bottom pegs drop into the alignment holes and the cartridge sits flush.
The brass retaining nut is threaded back over the cartridge by hand, then tightened down firmly with the adjustable wrench.
The decorative dome cap is screwed back on by hand, and the flat metal handle is pressed down onto the new cartridge stem.
The Allen wrench tightens the set screw clockwise, the red/blue plug is pushed back into the hole, and the handle is lifted to show water flowing.
